source_set.safe_takeaway: Treat Codex as a multi-surface coding agent spanning CLI, IDE, web/mobile, and SDK-style use; THOS runner design should preserve local verification and repo-grounded validation rather than assuming a single interface is canonical.
Documentation MCP should remain read-only and source-led; use it for source refresh and citation grounding, not account mutation or secret-bearing automation.
Shell-enabled agent work should keep a controlled plan-execute loop with sandboxing, allow/deny boundaries, and explicit user authority for risky actions.

The Codex CLI remains an open local terminal agent; install and update surfaces can differ across npm, release archives, and local binaries, so local version checks must be paired with source-drift receipts.
Release notes are useful for app-server, remote-control, sandbox, profile, MCP, and connector changes, but snippets can lag; do not overclaim current-latest status without direct live verification.
MCP integration should separate read-only source access from mutation-capable tools, with clear capability boundaries and per-server trust review.

source_drift_watch: Local CLI version evidence and public release snippets may disagree; prefer local command receipts for installed-version status and primary release pages for capability review.
Do not treat a single search snippet as current-latest truth.
Fold source refresh into THOS runner design only after preserving exact repo validation, raw-output boundaries, and open empirical/GMUT gates.
next_actions: Add source-refresh receipts during x2 synthesis when web research materially changes runner design.
Keep OpenAI/Codex, MCP, security, NVIDIA, Google Cloud, and GitHub/npm as prioritized primary-source lanes.
Use source refresh to improve command-index compatibility, app-server readiness, sandbox diagnostics, and multi-lane watcher behavior.
